title: Twenty-five
logline: Wood turns twenty-five. Gully brings a cake to the frame shop. The hours card is behind them, in focus.

panels.composition: The frame shop, Saturday, the only day Wood works now. GULLY in the door with a sheet cake. The OWNER at the mat cutter. WOOD. Behind them in the window: the HOURS card, legible.

image.prompt: a young man carrying a sheet cake with many candles into a picture-framing shop, the owner at a mat cutter objecting, another young man and a dog, an hours card visible in the window behind them, muddy digital flats

panels.composition: The cake on the counter. Twenty-five candles. Gully lighting them with a mat knife's lighter — no, a lighter. Wood.

balloons.text: A quarter century. Kafka was working at an insurance company at twenty-five.
You work at a frame shop two days a week.

image.prompt: close-up of a sheet cake with twenty-five candles being lit on a shop counter, a young man beside it saying something rueful

panels.composition: Wood blowing them out. The owner, despite herself, clapping once. The dog under the counter with a piece already.

image.prompt: a young man blowing out candles while the shop owner claps once despite herself and a dog under the counter already has a piece of cake, no words

panels.composition: The three of them eating cake off mat-board offcuts. The window. The card: TUES · SAT · 10–3. The strip puts the card dead center behind Wood's head.

image.prompt: three people eating cake off scraps of mat board in a frame shop, a hand-lettered hours card in the window centered directly behind the young man's head, no words
image.notes: Compose the card behind his head. The strip is telling you the hours without saying it.

art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays in watercolor, improving

notes: Twenty-five. Cake on offcuts. The hours card composed behind his head.
